about: Shared cross-language vectors for the ISO 10303-21 HEADER a STEP export writes.
Read by rust/export/tests/step_header_parity.rs (write_header, via export_step) and
by packages/export/src/step-header.parity.test.ts (buildStepHeader, via generateHeader).
`expectedHeader` is written from ISO 10303-21 and from each case's own source file,
NOT copied from either implementation's output. Part 21 clause 8 gives FILE_NAME as
(name, time_stamp, author, organization, preprocessor_version, originating_system,
authorization) and FILE_DESCRIPTION as (description, implementation_level); a value the
source stated is that file's, and an exporter that replaces it states something else.
Anchoring on the schema rather than on the sibling is deliberate: a test that compared
the two halves only to each other would go green the moment they were wrong the same way.
Precedence, identical on both sides: an explicit option wins, else the source header's
value, else the documented default (description 'Exported from ifc-lite',
implementation_level '2;1', name 'export.ifc', preprocessor_version 'ifc-lite',
originating_system = preprocessor_version, authorization '').
Every case states `options.timeStamp`. With none, the TypeScript half stamps the current
time and the Rust half carries the source's stamp forward (SystemTime::now is unavailable
on wasm32-unknown-unknown, the target that exporter ships to). That default is the one
documented difference between the halves and cannot be pinned by a fixture; stating a
stamp removes it, and every other field is compared.
Not pinned here, because the two halves genuinely disagree and the TypeScript half lives
in a package this fixture's author does not own: a header whose FILE_DESCRIPTION text
contains the literal 'ENDSEC' or the literal 'FILE_NAME'. The Rust reader skips quoted
text when it looks for those (as step_text::detect_schema already does); the TypeScript
reader's indexOf does not, and truncates or mis-locates the record. Rust is right there
and the difference is reported separately, not encoded as agreement.

cases.name: authored header round-trips field for field
cases.why: The source stated an MVD, an author, an organization, an authoring system and an authorization. Each is that file's own fact; an exporter that drops it, or writes a different MVD over it, is making a false statement about the model.

cases.name: no header records fall back to the documented defaults
cases.why: Negative control for the case above: with nothing to preserve, both halves must write the SAME defaults, and the default FILE_DESCRIPTION item must not assert a model view definition the file never claimed.

cases.name: explicit options override the source header
cases.why: Negative control for echoing: a half that simply copied the source through would fail every overridden field here. Note authorization and originating_system have no option and stay the source's.

cases.name: commas, parentheses and doubled apostrophes inside quoted values
cases.why: Part 21 6.3.2.4 writes a literal apostrophe doubled, so a splitter blind to quote state cuts 'CoordinateReference [Origin (0,0,0), Site]' into three items and loses O'Brien. The empty organization list is load-bearing too: a list the source stated as empty is not the same as one it never stated, and only the latter is back-filled with ('').

cases.name: non-ASCII is decoded on read and re-encoded on write
cases.why: Part 21 6.3.3.4 limits a literal's plain-text bytes to 32-126, so 'Muller' with an umlaut must leave as \X2\00FC\X0\ whether it arrived raw or already encoded. Both halves must therefore DECODE the source value and re-encode it, not copy the bytes: a half that copied would emit raw UTF-8 for the first author, and a half that re-escaped without decoding would double the backslashes of the second.
